Apply the Saint-Venant isentropic flow relations to a subsonic flow at M = 0.5, not the Rayleigh-Pitot formula, since no detached shock is present in subsonic flow.

Use the working fluid as standard air with γ = 1.4 and R = 287 J/(kg·K).

Compute the stagnation-to-static temperature ratio as T₀/T = 1 + ((γ − 1)/2) × M².

Compute the stagnation-to-static pressure ratio as p₀/p = (T₀/T)^(γ/(γ − 1)).

Compute the stagnation-to-static density ratio as ρ₀/ρ = (T₀/T)^(1/(γ − 1)).

Substitute M = 0.5 and γ = 1.4 into all three expressions.

Report T₀/T = 1.0500.

Report p₀/p ≈ 1.1862.

Report ρ₀/ρ ≈ 1.1297.

Note that these are dimensionless ratios, so no additional reference pressure, temperature, or density is required.

Present the three results clearly together so they can be cross-checked using p₀/p = (ρ₀/ρ)^γ.
